## [#10936 - NumberParser corrupts Arabic-digit numbers with locale-specific separators](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10936)

- **Problem:** **High severity.** Applications parsing their own formatted numbers can silently accept a different numeric value in Sindhi and other Arabic-digit locales. The author reports Sindhi `1234.5` round-tripping as "`12345`", USD `12.5` as "`1250`", Punjabi `0.25` as "`25`", and Urdu input returning `NaN`. Potential quantity/currency corruption warrants priority; persisted data loss is not established.
- **Concerns / notes:** Reading only. The report provides a small standalone API reproduction, expected/actual values, package 3.6.9, the exact current-main commit, Node 26.13.0 / ICU 78.3 / CLDR 48.0 and Debian 12. It says the script ran directly against main, but that claim was not independently verified. No hosted runnable reproduction is supplied.
- **Source / duplicates:** [NumberParser.ts lines 256-265](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/@internationalized/number/src/NumberParser.ts#L256-L265) unconditionally maps comma/U+060C to the decimal symbol and period to the group symbol for `arab`; it does not exclude characters already serving as the locale's separator. This supports the proposed cause, not the runtime output. Closed [#10875](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10875) instead describes a period-only edit that changes the numbering system "while the numeric value remains 1"; it is not this formatted-value corruption. Merged [#8592](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/8592) addresses other parser bugs and does not establish a fix for this case. Open/closed issue and PR searches found no supported duplicate or matching complete fix.
- **Maintainer next step:** **Ready for review: yes**, from sufficient standalone reproduction detail and complete runtime information. Investigate separator preservation across the reported locales and currency/default grouping options, while retaining Arabic keyboard fallback support. A maintainer should request a StackBlitz or CodeSandbox containing the standalone case, rather than accepting "Not applicable" as a runnable reproduction. Browser/ICU coverage remains unmeasured. No verified API-only workaround or earlier working version is established; do not advise switching the user's locale or stripping separators.

### Would have done

- **Labels (proposed):** Would add `bug`, `internationalization`, `NumberField` (downstream numeric-input impact), `needs investigation`, `ready for review`, and `ai-reviewed`. Would remove none. All exist in the live inventory. No `RAC` or `S2`: the defect is reported in the lower-level `@internationalized/number` package. Would not add `regression` without an earlier working version.
- **Maintainer action:** Would prioritise round-trip correctness and request the hosted reproduction above; would not put this on author wait because investigation can proceed from the supplied detail.
- **Comment / closure:** Would post no comment or duplicate notice and would not close.

## [#10937 - Sheet enter-edge observation strands the overlay; early Select popover becomes inert](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10937)

- **Problem:** **High severity.** A partially visible Sheet can reportedly remain over the page after dismissal, and a Select opened during entry can become non-interactive. The report says "the page stays inert until one tap anywhere closes it" in the iPhone-platform WebKit case and that a Select option tap "closes the list with no choice made" in Chromium. Modal interaction and accessibility are affected; the extra tap/retry is not a complete fix.
- **Concerns / notes:** Reading only. The author reports RAC 1.22.1 / hooks package 3.53.1, Playwright 1.64.1 Chromium 156 and WebKit on Windows 11, with emulated iPhone geometry/platform rather than a real device. The enter failure reportedly occurred in "3 of 325 rounds"; partial `snapPoints` and increased frequency on main are explicitly predictions, not measured results. Detailed steps are present, but there is no runnable hosted fixture. Do not run the proposed prototype wrappers or instrumentation.
- **Source evidence:** [Sheet.tsx lines 285-303](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L285-L303) reads `intersectionRatio > 0` with `threshold: [0, 1]`; [lines 414-430](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L414-L430) wait for `scrollend` on desktop Safari when visibility is false. Merged [#10815](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10815) says "Jump to where the sheet's leading edge meets the viewport"; that helper remains on [main, lines 1136-1153](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L1136-L1153). This makes the enter-boundary concern credible, but does not prove frequency or a regression.
- **Nested-overlay evidence / duplicates:** [useModalOverlay.ts lines 85-94](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/overlays/useModalOverlay.ts#L85-L94) defers the hide until entered; [ariaHideOutside.ts lines 50-56 and 300-307](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/overlays/ariaHideOutside.ts#L300-L307) creates a new target set while `keepVisible` registers only with the current observer. Closed [#10814](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10814) matches the second defect: "The list is made inert" when the deferred modal hide runs after the popover. Its [final author comment](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10814#issuecomment-6292702153) accepts duplicate closure under [#10802](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10802), so do not silently overturn that disposition. However, #10802 and open [#10812](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10812) / [#10884](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10884) describe shared hide-channel restoration, not a complete fix for entry-order visibility. The new enter-edge defect also differs from [#10897](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10897)'s batched exit reports and [#10877](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10877)'s scroll writes during exit. No supported whole-issue duplicate or complete fix was found.
- **Maintainer next step:** **Ready for review: yes**, with enough geometry, timing, symptoms and environment detail to investigate. Request a hosted StackBlitz/CodeSandbox for each defect and determine whether to split the entry-order case after comparing #10814 / #10802. Verify partial/full-height sheets, detents, entry/exit boundaries and nested Select/ComboBox on current main and real Safari/iOS. Do not endorse the internal top-layer attribute or a timing workaround. Neither observer candidate has been validated; the author's `isIntersecting` candidate explicitly has a full-height exit caveat.

### Would have done

- **Labels (proposed):** Would add `bug`, `Sheet`, `Select`, `Overlays`, `RAC`, `accessibility` (reported inert/non-interactive modal content), `needs investigation`, `ready for review`, and `ai-reviewed`. Would remove none. All exist. Would not add `duplicate` to this mixed report, `browser bug` without establishing browser responsibility, or `regression` from an unmeasured main-frequency prediction.
- **Maintainer action:** Would prioritise dismissal and nested-overlay accessibility, request the two hosted cases, and preserve the distinct entry-edge defect while deciding how to consolidate the matching nested-overlay evidence.
- **Comment / closure:** Would post no duplicate notice for the whole issue and would not close. Prior duplicate acceptance on #10814 is context, not proof that #10937 is resolved.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Current source supports both mechanisms, but edge-observer behaviour, real-device impact and whether the open hide-channel fixes affect the Select case require runtime evidence.

## [#10935 - NumberField blur during CalendarCell focus warns and loses correction announcements](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10935)

- **Problem:** **Medium severity, accessibility-impacting.** Moving from a NumberField to a Calendar date reportedly commits a clamped value without announcing the correction. The author says typing `9` with `maxValue={8}` clamps to `8` "with no announcement; leaving with Tab announces '8'." This is more than a development warning, but no lost stored value or crash is established.
- **Concerns / notes:** Reading only. A [StackBlitz link](https://stackblitz.com/edit/dccr7arv), concrete click steps, expected/actual behaviour, RAC 1.22.1, hooks 3.53.1, React/React DOM 19.3.1, Chrome and Windows 11 are supplied. The reporter uses HeroUI 3 and verifies the announcement claim through a jsdom live region, not a real screen reader; the hosted reproduction was not opened.
- **Source / duplicate evidence:** [useNumberField.ts lines 134-150](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/numberfield/useNumberField.ts#L134-L150) synchronously commits on blur, then announces only if the DOM input differs from the old value. [useCalendarCell.ts lines 322-325](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/calendar/useCalendarCell.ts#L322-L325) moves focus from an effect. Open [#10044](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10044) quotes the same "flushSync was called from inside a lifecycle method" warning when disabling a focused NumberField; a [maintainer comment](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10044#issuecomment-4427693909) identifies "stale closures" and "event timing". This supports shared NumberField commit-timing investigation, but the Calendar trigger and lost announcement are additional evidence, not the disabling-specific stale-value case. [#10861](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10861) is closed and unmerged; its proposed disabled-input guard is not an available fix for this active-input blur.
- **Maintainer next step:** **Ready for review: yes.** Verify the Calendar-triggered blur in a minimal direct RAC composition and real browser/assistive-technology combination, retaining the clamped-value announcement as an acceptance criterion. Consolidate with #10044 only after recording this distinct trigger and accessibility evidence there; closure is a maintainer decision after that, not an automatic duplicate disposition. No verified accessible API-only workaround or previously working version is established.

### Would have done

- **Labels (proposed):** Would add `bug`, `NumberField`, `Calendar`, `RAC`, `accessibility`, `needs investigation`, `ready for review`, and `ai-reviewed`. Would remove none. All exist. Would defer `duplicate` until a maintainer confirms consolidation; would not add `regression`.
- **Duplicate notice (proposed):** "This appears to share the NumberField blur/flushSync timing problem tracked in [#10044](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10044). This report adds a CalendarCell focus trigger and lost corrected-value announcement, which should be retained when investigating the fix." No existing notice is present on #10935. Would draft only this supported relationship notice, not an information-request comment.
- **Maintainer action / closure:** Would recommend the focused accessibility investigation and conditional consolidation above; would not close.
- **Confidence:** Medium on duplicate disposition: source and the identical warning support a common path, but #10044 also has disabling-specific stale closures, and the additional announcement failure has not been independently measured.

## [#10934 - Toolbar redirects a click's focus to the previously focused item](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10934)

- **Problem:** **Medium severity, accessibility-impacting.** Mixed pointer/keyboard users reportedly activate one Toolbar item while focus returns to another, making subsequent navigation and visible focus misleading. The author says "visually first widget was toggled, but second widget actually has focus".
- **Concerns / notes:** Reading only. The report supplies exact tab/arrow/click steps against the first public docs example, inline composition, Firefox/Chrome/Safari and macOS Tahoe 26.7.1. RAC 1.22.0 is an assumption about the docs deployment, not a verified deployed version. Videos and the docs URL were not opened. No hosted runnable reproduction is supplied, but the explicit public-example steps are sufficient to begin investigation.
- **Source / existing fix:** [useToolbar.ts lines 131-154](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/toolbar/useToolbar.ts#L131-L154) restores the previous item in capture-phase focus handling without distinguishing a pointer entry. Open [#10938](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10938), created November 7 at `16:09:39Z`, explicitly says "Closes #10934". Its GET-read patch gates restoration on `isFocusVisible()` and adds clicked-item/keyboard-return assertions. It is **not merged or validated by this triage**; do not tell the author it is released. Open [#5457](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/5457) instead reports "two items receive the focus event" on keyboard entry with custom handlers; closed, unmerged [#5463](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/5463) does not establish a fix for the present pointer-redirection case. No duplicate closure recommendation is warranted.
- **Maintainer next step:** **Ready for review: yes; matching fix already open.** Review #10938 for pointer focus preservation and keyboard restoration, including nested groups and the reported browsers. A maintainer should request a StackBlitz/CodeSandbox with the docs example and confirm the affected package version if the current source cannot reproduce it. Keep #10934 open pending the linked fix; do not launch a second implementation or suggest consumer focus overrides.

### Would have done

- **Labels (proposed):** Would add `bug`, `Toolbar`, `RAC`, `accessibility`, `ready for review`, `waiting for maintainer` (matching PR needs maintainer review), and `ai-reviewed`. Would remove none. All exist. Would not add `regression` without an earlier working version.
- **Maintainer action:** Would direct review to #10938 and verify its keyboard/pointer cases; the fix patch is evidence of ongoing work, not proof the issue is solved.
- **Comment / closure:** Would post no comment or duplicate notice and would not close before the matching fix lands.
